contract.name: G(d, b)
contract.NLL: q_k >= exp(-d) p_k for every class k
contract.Brier: sum_k q_k^2 - sum_k p_k^2 - 2 (q_y - p_y) <= b for every label y
contract.Class: q has the strict argmax d(p) (numpy argmax of p, first index)
contract.bin: admissible iff one q satisfies G for every member; necessary: sum_k max_member p_k <= exp(d)

conventions.recipients: recipient 1 stands for income (K = 2); recipient 2 stands for occupation, with K = 3 in every law (the real occupation recipient has K = 6)
conventions.reference_vectors: exact rationals (strings) with their float64 values (p*_float = float(rational)); every vector is positive with a strict argmax
conventions.partition_domain: a release partitions the DISTINCT reference values of a recipient (inputs with equal vectors always share a token)
conventions.capacity: 8 tokens per predicted class (recipient 1) / 64 (recipient 2); no law has more than 6 inputs, so the capacity bound never binds
conventions.sex: sex1 = P(SEX = 1 | x); P = P(x); exact rationals
conventions.measures: plug-in mutual information in nats (natural log) and exact Bayes accuracy of SEX from t1, t2, (t1, t2)
conventions.capability_not_prevalence: purpose-built fixtures: they show that the oracles can detect each situation, not how often it occurs in real data

NULL.name: NULL
NULL.intended_property: Privacy cannot usefully improve under G: every SEX-informative distinction lies between reference vectors too far apart to merge (sum_k max p_k > e^d), in both recipients; every admissible bin is SEX-homogeneous, so every admissible deterministic partition (and every stochastic channel whose supported outputs satisfy G) leaves I(S;t1), I(S;t2) and I(S;t1,t2) at their identity values.
NULL.design: x0/x1 (SEX law 4/5) and x2/x3 (1/5) are mergeable pairs (TV 0.001-0.002) in both recipients; every pair with different SEX laws is >= 0.018 apart in total variation (sum_k max >= 1.018 > e^d = 1.0050125) or has a different decision (x4, x5 are class 1 in recipient 1 and class 2 in recipient 2, 0.02 apart).

2.stands_for: occupation (real K=6; K=3 in the laws)

POSITIVE.name: POSITIVE
POSITIVE.intended_property: Admissible coarsening removes an unnecessary sensitive distinction: in each recipient x1 and x2 differ in SEX law (1/5 vs 4/5) but their reference vectors are mergeable under G; the privacy-aware local partition {x0},{x1,x2},{x3} halves the SEX information of the chain, while the unique fewest-token (task-only) partition {x0,x1},{x2,x3} keeps it.
POSITIVE.design: x0..x3 form a chain in each recipient (consecutive TV 0.003: sum_k max = 1.003 <= e^d, mergeable; two steps apart TV 0.006: sum_k max = 1.006 > e^d, certified infeasible), so the admissible bins of the chain are the three adjacent pairs; the fewest-token partition of the chain is unique ({x0,x1},{x2,x3}, SEX-homogeneous). x4/x5 (SEX law 1/2, decision class 1) are a SEX-neutral mergeable pair.

2.stands_for: occupation (real K=6; K=3 in the laws)

COMPLEMENTARY.name: COMPLEMENTARY
COMPLEMENTARY.intended_property: XOR coalition clue: recipient 1 is forced to disclose a (x0,x1 vs x2,x3; non-mergeable) and recipient 2 is forced to disclose b (x0,x2 vs x1,x3; different decisions); SEX law 9/10 if a = b and 1/10 otherwise. Each recipient alone leaks SEX through mergeable sub-distinctions, which admissible (local) merging removes completely, but the pair (t1, t2) still reveals (a, b) and hence SEX for every admissible pair of partitions.
COMPLEMENTARY.design: a = 0 for x0, x1 and a = 1 for x2, x3; b = 0 for x0, x2 and b = 1 for x1, x3. Recipient 1: within-a pairs are 0.002 apart (mergeable), across a >= 0.048 apart (certified infeasible), one decision class (CLASS ineligible). Recipient 2: within-b pairs 0.001 apart (mergeable), b = 0 is class 0 and b = 1 is class 1 (CLASS eligible).

2.stands_for: occupation (real K=6; K=3 in the laws)

NO_COALITION.name: NO_COALITION
NO_COALITION.intended_property: No extra coalition clue: SEX depends only on a, recipient 1 sees only a, recipient 2 sees only b, and b is independent of (a, SEX); for every admissible pair of partitions I(S;t1,t2) = I(S;t1) = the better single release. Recipient 1 still has local headroom (a = 0 and a = 1 are mergeable).
NO_COALITION.design: inputs (a, b): x0 (0,0), x1 (0,1), x2 (1,0), x3 (1,1), x4 (2,0), x5 (2,1); P uniform, so a and b are independent. p1 depends on a only (a = 0, 1 mergeable, 0.002 apart; a = 2 class 1); p2 depends on b only (b = 0 class 0, b = 1 class 2). SEX law 4/5, 1/5, 3/5 for a = 0, 1, 2.

2.stands_for: occupation (real K=6; K=3 in the laws)

JOINT_HEADROOM.name: JOINT_HEADROOM
JOINT_HEADROOM.intended_property: Coordination headroom: the best admissible JOINT pair of partitions has strictly lower coalition MI I(S; t1, t2) than the local design and than BOTH non-adaptive sequential designs (1->2 and 2->1), for every tie choice. The only coalition-reducing move hides the x1/x2 distinction (SEX law 1/10 vs 4/5) from BOTH recipients; each recipient on its own prefers a different merge that the other recipient's geometry makes useless to the coalition, so local, 1->2 and 2->1 all leave the coalition at I(S;X).
JOINT_HEADROOM.design: Recipient 1 (K = 2): chain x2 - x1 - x3 at (0.900, 0.100), (0.903, 0.097), (0.906, 0.094) (consecutive sum_k max = 1.003, mergeable; two steps 1.006, certified infeasible); x0 at (0.950, 0.050) is >= 0.044 away (certified infeasible with every chain value). Recipient 2 (K = 3): chain {x1} - {x0, x2} - {x3} at (0.800, 0.150, 0.050), (0.803, 0.147, 0.050), (0.806, 0.144, 0.050) (x0 and x2 share one reference vector). Own-MI optima: recipient 1 merges {x1, x3}; recipient 2 merges {x0, x2} with {x3}. Neither merge can reduce the coalition (recipient 2 never merges x1 with x3; recipient 1 never merges x0, x2, x3 together), and each first mover's own optimum keeps x1 and x2 apart, so the second mover cannot help. The joint optimum merges {x1, x2} for recipient 1 and {x1} with {x0, x2} for recipient 2.
JOINT_HEADROOM.capacity: the registered i8o64 bound: at most 8 tokens per predicted class for recipient 1 and 64 for recipient 2 (never binds: recipient 1 has 4 values in one class, recipient 2 has 3)
JOINT_HEADROOM.tie_rule: own-MI argmins are compared within 1e-12; every tied choice is evaluated and the claim must hold against the most favourable one (here every own-MI argmin and the joint argmin are unique, so no tie-break is involved); the second mover's coalition-MI minimum is a single value

arms.sequential_1_to_2: recipient 1 its own-MI minimum, then recipient 2 the partition minimising I(S; t1, t2) given recipient 1's PARTITION (non-adaptive)
arms.joint: minimum of I(S; t1, t2) over all admissible pairs

2.stands_for: occupation (real K=6; K=3 in the laws)

construction_check_rule: ccm.data.toy_law_check (role F; independent of ccm.guard/geometry/oracle): every subset of distinct reference values is CERTIFIED (q given; exact rational check with a rigorous bracket of exp(-d) AND float64 check with no tolerance, every member and every label), INFEASIBLE_CLASS or INFEASIBLE_NLL (sum_k max > exp(d)); zero UNDECIDED subsets is required. MI ties within 1e-12 are reported as ranges. Reproduce with `PYTHONPATH=. python -m ccm.data toy-laws-check`.

witnesses.tie_rule: every own-MI argmin of the first mover (ties within 1e-12) is listed; the second mover's coalition-MI minimum is a single value whatever its tie-break

amendments.change: added the law JOINT_HEADROOM (coordination headroom: joint < local, sequential 1->2 and 2->1)
amendments.reason: the four original laws contain no fixture in which the joint arm strictly beats the local and both sequential arms (COMPLEMENTARY's coalition clue is forced), so the coalition-aware arms were tested only as equalities; added before any candidate code evaluated any law
